title: Count Beautiful Splits in an Array
summary: Given an array nums, count the number of ways it can be split into three subarrays nums1, nums2, and nums3 such that nums1 is a prefix of nums2 or nums2 is a prefix of nums3, and the subarrays are formed by concatenating nums1, nums2, and nums3 in that order.
statement: Given an array nums, count the number of ways it can be split into three subarrays nums1, nums2, and nums3 such that nums1 is a prefix of nums2 or nums2 is a prefix of nums3, and the subarrays are formed by concatenating nums1, nums2, and nums3 in that order.
constraints: Split it into three nonempty consecutive parts.
Count splits where the first part prefixes the second or the second prefixes the third.
hints: Both conditions are longest-common-prefix queries between fixed suffix starts.
Use Z-values for the whole array and separately for each suffix while retaining only linear memory.
Enumerate both cuts; test prefix lengths from the appropriate Z arrays and add their logical union.
Z-values give exact matching-prefix lengths, and every ordered pair of nonempty cuts is examined once.
editorial: Z-values give exact matching-prefix lengths, and every ordered pair of nonempty cuts is examined once.

tests.explanation: The two valid cut pairs satisfy one of the required prefix relationships.
The only split has all singleton parts, so both prefix conditions hold and it counts once.
